REASONING:
Step 1 – Project framing  
- **Objective / PDO:** Improve access to water supply and sanitation services, integrated water resources management, and operational performance of service providers.  
- **Scope & components:** Four components – (1) WSS in small towns & Rural Growth Centres (RGCs) + support to districts hosting refugees; (2) WSS in large towns + refugee districts; (3) Water resources management (catchment measures, groundwater study, WIS); (4) Project implementation & institutional strengthening.  
- **Delivery model:** Implemented by two IAs – Ministry of Water & Environment (MWE) and National Water & Sewerage Corporation (NWSC). Regional Umbrella Water Authorities (UWAs) manage small‑town schemes; NWSC manages large towns; extensive coordination through WESLD, WESWG and a Project Support Team.  
- **Timeline:** Effective 14 Jun 2018, expected closing 02 Dec 2024 (≈ 6 years).  
- **Budget / financing:** Total US $313 m (IDA credit $251 m, IDA grant $29 m, KfW $25 m, counterpart $8 m).  
- **Key stakeholders:** GoU (MWE, NWSC, MoFPED, OPM), UNHCR, donors (KfW, AfDB), local authorities, community groups, UWAs, World Bank.  
- **External dependencies / risks:** Regional instability (South‑Sudan conflict), large refugee influx, climate variability (floods/droughts), donor funding timelines, IFMS financial‑reporting system not fully operational.

Step 2 – Category sweep (candidate risks with supporting evidence)

| ID | Category | Description (evidence) |
|----|----------|------------------------|
| R01 | technical | “Incomplete needs assessment and inadequate attention to geotechnical studies … resulting in design changes/variations during construction and consequently time and cost overruns.” |
| R02 | technical | “Limited domestic contracting capacity to conduct projects of this nature, complexity, and scope; most contracts will be done by international firms.” |
| R03 | environmental | “Extreme temperature will likely trigger increased evapotranspiration and precipitation variability, leading to floods that can damage infrastructure.” |
| R04 | technical | “Namatala’s dry weather flows … may not be sufficient to meet projected water demand and maintain an adequate EF.” |
| R05 | financial | “UWAs can cover their routine O&M costs, but they do not generate enough revenue to cover capital investments.” |
| R06 | financial | “Annual payments of principal and service charge would correspond to less than 1.4 % of total revenues after 2025.” |
| R07 | financial | “Project module of the IFMS is not yet fully operational … increases the risk of errors and inaccuracy of financial reports.” |
| R08 | schedule | “PDU staff have no experience in using World Bank Procurement Regulations and have a heavy workload; leads to delays.” |
| R09 | schedule | “Delays in preparing specifications, statement of requirements, and ToR by the User Departments.” |
| R10 | stakeholder | “Estimated one million South Sudanese refugees have already migrated to Uganda, placing excessive pressure on Uganda’s public services and natural resources.” |
| R11 | stakeholder | “Women and girls bear the heaviest burden for water collection; long walks trigger GBV such as sexual assaults.” |
| R12 | stakeholder | “Given the number of departments … the MWE’s WESLD will take the responsibility for overall coordination and communication.” |
| R13 | political_regulatory | “The most critical risk to this outlook is regional instability, particularly from the ongoing conflict in South Sudan.” |
| R15 | environmental | “Management measures for the removal, packaging, transportation and disposal of existing asbestos waste, following additional guidance that will be provided by NEMA.” |
| R16 | organizational | “Turnover of qualified and experienced staff is noticed.” |
| R17 | organizational | “Ministry internal audit review reports are not shared regularly with the World Bank.” |

Step 3 – Evidence filter  
All listed risks are directly supported by the quoted statements; none were discarded.

Step 4 – Assessment & mitigation  

| ID | Likelihood (1‑5) | Impact (1‑5) | Mitigation (concise) |
|----|------------------|--------------|----------------------|
| R01 | 3 | 4 | Conduct thorough design reviews, include contingency budgets, engage experienced consultants, and enforce strict change‑control procedures. |
| R02 | 3 | 3 | Perform market sounding, allow joint‑venture bids, and provide capacity‑building for local firms. |
| R03 | 3 | 4 | Integrate climate‑resilient designs, flood protection, buffer zones and early‑warning systems into all infrastructure. |
| R04 | 3 | 3 | Complete the Augmented Water Supply Study and consider storage or alternative sources to guarantee minimum environmental flow. |
| R05 | 3 | 4 | Set up a revolving fund, adjust tariffs for full cost recovery, and secure additional donor financing for capital works. |
| R06 | 2 | 3 | Phase debt service, align repayments with cash‑flow forecasts, and keep a reserve fund for contingencies. |
| R07 | 3 | 3 | Prioritise full activation of the IFMS project module, train finance staff and apply manual cross‑checks during transition. |
| R08 | 4 | 3 | Recruit procurement consultants, provide targeted World Bank procurement training, and augment PDU staffing. |
| R09 | 3 | 3 | Assign a dedicated technical team to draft specifications early and use standard templates for ToRs. |
| R10 | 4 | 4 | Coordinate with UNHCR/OPM to integrate refugee water needs, expand supply capacity and develop a refugee water tariff. |
| R11 | 3 | 3 | Install piped water points nearer households, ensure gender‑segregated facilities and conduct GBV awareness/training. |
| R12 | 3 | 3 | Create a formal inter‑agency coordination framework with regular meetings and clear roles for WESLD and focal points. |
| R13 | 3 | 4 | Monitor regional security, develop contingency plans and maintain dialogue with donors to adjust implementation as needed. |
| R15 | 2 | 3 | Follow NEMA asbestos‑handling guidelines, embed safe removal/disposal procedures in contracts and train workers on hazardous‑material safety. |
| R16 | 3 | 3 | Introduce staff‑retention incentives, succession planning and knowledge‑management systems. |
| R17 | 3 | 3 | Establish a schedule for timely sharing of internal‑audit reports with the World Bank and assign a liaison officer. |

Step 5 – Consolidation  
All 16 risks are distinct and retained.
